CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to reassess management of anxiety, sleep disturbances, persistent fatigue, and headache symptoms.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for a follow-up appointment, reporting a mixed response to the recent adjustments in his treatment regimen. He notes that although his sleep quality remains relatively stable with an average of 7.5 hours per night, he still struggles with sleep onset, particularly on nights preceding demanding workdays. The trazodone at 75 mg continues to facilitate nocturnal awakenings, but he reports increased episodes of early morning awakenings, which leave him feeling unrested.
In terms of his persistent fatigue, Mr. Smith describes a slight improvement in his daytime energy levels, attributing this to his enhanced mindfulness practices and regular yoga sessions. However, he still experiences significant fatigue during peak work periods, which he describes as mentally exhausting. His headache symptoms have remained consistent, occurring approximately three times per week, with a reported intensity of 5-7 out of 10. He has been utilizing ibuprofen 400 mg approximately 4-5 times weekly for headache relief, which he states has been somewhat effective but is concerned about the increased reliance on this medication.
Mr. Smith has continued his commitment to his holistic treatment plan, including acupuncture sessions and yoga classes. He has also engaged in additional cognitive-behavioral therapy sessions, which he feels have been beneficial in managing his anxiety, particularly regarding work stressors. He expresses a desire to further develop coping strategies to handle the pressures associated with his job.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 200 mg daily 2. Trazodone 75 mg at bedtime 3. Melatonin 10 mg at bedtime 4. Lisinopril 10 mg daily 5. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief (increased usage noted) 6. Amitriptyline 40 mg nightly 7. Topiramate 25 mg daily (newly initiated) 8. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (usage stable)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to work as a software engineer, reporting that the pressure from project deadlines remains a significant stressor. He actively participates in yoga and meditation, which he finds helpful. He abstains from alcohol and follows a primarily plant-based diet, although he admits to occasionally indulging in processed foods during particularly stressful weeks.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Sleep initiation difficulties persist; anxiety is stable with slight improvements noted; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms reported. - Neurological: Headache frequency remains consistent; intensity fluctuates; no visual changes or neurological deficits. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Persistent fatigue; no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 120/76 mmHg, HR 70 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.4F - General: Alert, oriented, and appears fatigued but in no acute distress. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears stable with noted fatigue.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 200 mg daily. Reinforce tapering of lorazepam use as needed. Encourage ongoing cognitive-behavioral therapy sessions to enhance coping strategies for work-related stress. 2. Insomnia: Maintain trazodone at 75 mg; continue melatonin at 10 mg; explore sleep hygiene strategies and consider a sleep study if sleep onset issues persist. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue amitriptyline at 40 mg nightly. Given the increased frequency and intensity of headaches, continue topiramate at 25 mg daily, with plans to titrate based on symptom response. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Encourage continued physical activity and mindfulness practices. Refer to a nutritionist for dietary optimization, particularly during high-stress periods.
Follow-up appointment scheduled for 2028-08-01 to assess ongoing symptoms, evaluate treatment efficacy, and make further medication adjustments as necessary. Mr. Smith is advised to contact the office sooner if he experiences any exacerbation of symptoms or adverse effects from medications.
